    - "READ DES-076 IN DESIGN.md FIRST, specifically its 'Non-goal' section. You wrote it. It contains the design for this mission — the bind-provenance field and the narrowly-gated per-delegation disclaim — and the reasoning for why a blanket bypass flag is forbidden. This contract funds exactly the follow-up DES-076 recommends. Do not redesign it from scratch; do challenge it if implementation reveals the recommendation was wrong, and say so explicitly rather than silently diverging."
    - "REQUIREMENT: `ethos mission abandon` must be able to retire a mission whose ONLY delegation is one wrongly attributed to it by a dispatch-sidecar capture, WITHOUT weakening Store.Abandon's existing all-delegations-block gate or its result gate. Abandon's own doc comment rejects a bypass flag because 'the gate is the whole point' — honor that. The disclaim must be operator-named, per-delegation, and checked MECHANICALLY against recorded provenance, never inferred by heuristic and never a blanket flag."
    - "PART 1 — record the fact that does not exist today. Tier alone cannot distinguish how a delegation was bound: explicit MISSION_ID env, inheritance from a parent, and dispatch-sidecar consumption all produce Tier B. Add a bind-provenance field to DelegationSkeleton (written by dispatchTierB) and Delegation. Enumerate the origins as a closed set with an explicit zero value for records written before this change — a pre-existing delegation must NOT be silently treated as disclaimable just because its provenance is unknown. State in your result what the unknown case does and why that direction is the safe one."
    - "PART 2 — the retirement path. A new narrowly-gated method (or an explicit parameter on Abandon) that accepts an operator-named delegation ID, verifies mechanically that its recorded provenance is dispatch-sidecar capture, and only then permits the retirement. A delegation whose provenance is explicit-env or inherited must be refused with an actionable error naming why. Surface it on the CLI and, for parity, the MCP surface (DES-020: every MCP tool needs a formatter in format_output.go before shipping — check whether this change requires one)."
    - "BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY is a first-class requirement, not a footnote. Delegation records already exist on disk in this repo and in every consumer. Adding a field must not break reading them, and must not change how an existing record is treated. Verify by reading real on-disk delegation records from .punt-labs/ethos/missions/ BEFORE and AFTER your change and confirming identical interpretation. Paste the evidence."
    - "Every behavioural change needs a regression test verified FAILING against pre-fix code before the fix lands. At minimum: (a) a captured delegation CAN be disclaimed and the mission then abandoned; (b) a genuine explicit-env delegation CANNOT be disclaimed and abandon still refuses; (c) a pre-existing record with unknown provenance CANNOT be disclaimed; (d) disclaim does not bypass the result gate. State which you confirmed red first and the pre-fix failure output."
    - "SECURITY REVIEW YOUR OWN CHANGE before reporting. You are adding an operator-facing path that relaxes a deliberate guard. Ask explicitly: can this be used to retire a mission that genuinely had a worker do work? Can a malformed or hand-edited provenance field on disk unlock the path? Does the disclaim leave an audit record of who disclaimed what and why? Report your answers; 'I checked and found nothing' is only credible if you say what you checked for."
    - "make check green before EVERY commit. No suppressions. Note that make check does NOT catch every class — it missed Go doc-comment misattachment on PR #508 — so if you change a class it does not cover, say which verification you used instead and paste its output."
    - "GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./... must exit 0."
    - "The leader cannot run the setsid-detached test gate in this sandboxed session (the guard blocks setsid and env wrappers), so CI is the authoritative no-Claude-ancestor check. Do not assume a local pass means a CI pass — flag anything you believe is environment-sensitive so the leader watches for it specifically."
    - "Amend DES-076 with the outcome — it is currently marked PARTIAL precisely because this half was blocked. When this lands, its Non-goal section is no longer accurate. Update the heading and the section rather than appending a contradicting paragraph; an ADR that says two different things is worse than one that says nothing."
    - "CHANGELOG under [Unreleased]. User-visible: a mission wrongly captured by a dispatch sidecar can now be retired."
    - "Commit incrementally — one commit per logical step. Each commit passes make check. Do not accumulate more than 30 minutes of uncommitted changes."
    - "Do NOT push. Report and the leader pushes."
budget:
    rounds: 3
    reflection_after_each: true
context: |
    Second half of ethos-7tqd, and the last open item in the ethos
    cluster-2 bug triage. Continue on branch fix/spawn-binding in the
    session-pid-identity worktree, on top of commit 3cf6bf4.

    Mission m-2026-09-08-003 delivered the first half — the dispatch
    sidecar is now single-use and scoped to the contract's declared
    Worker, so the general "any next spawn gets captured" class is gone.
    It was closed as ESCALATED because its write-set covered internal/hook
    but the second requirement necessarily lives in internal/mission. That
    was the leader's scoping error, not a worker shortfall; the escalate
    verdict was the correct response and this contract is the correction.

    Why this half is still worth funding rather than deferring: DES-076
    honestly names the residual case it does not close — a spawn whose
    agent type EQUALS the dispatched Worker but whose task is unrelated.
    In this repo that is not an exotic edge case. The leader dispatches to
    bwk repeatedly, so same-type unrelated spawns are the common shape,
    and when one captures, the affected mission becomes unretireable. The
    cleanup path is what makes the residual survivable.

    Two lessons from PR #508's ten review rounds, both directly relevant:

    1. A comment describing what the code USED to do is a defect. Four
       rounds went to stale comments there, and one stale claim was
       hiding a real correctness bug — writing down WHY forced a claim
       precise enough to falsify. DES-076's PARTIAL marking and Non-goal
       section become stale the moment this lands; updating them is part
       of the work, not cleanup after it.

    2. Validate a detector before trusting a clean result. If you sweep
       for other call sites or other bypass paths, first confirm your
       method fires on the known-bad case. "I searched and found nothing"
       is worthless if the search could not have found anything.

tool_input.message:
Escalation accepted, and it was the right call. Requirement 1 is verified and I'm taking it to PR. Requirement 2 is funded as a new mission with the write-set you asked for.

**On the escalation.** The scoping error was mine, not yours. I wrote a contract whose second requirement necessarily lives in `store.go` and `delegation.go` and then handed you a write-set that excluded both. You did exactly what the contract told you to do when scope is wrong — escalate with evidence rather than work around it — and you enumerated why each workaround was unsafe (deleting delegation records destroys the audit trail the bead calls the product; `Store.Update` bypasses the lock, redaction, and result gates). That reasoning is what made this a two-minute decision instead of an argument.

`m-2026-09-08-003` is closed as escalated with a reflection recording it as a leader scoping error.

**Independent verification of requirement 1:** `make check` fully green including the race detector, `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` exit 0. I read DES-076 end to end. It's the standard I want — particularly that it names the residual case it does NOT close rather than implying the class is shut.

**Your new mission is `m-2026-09-08-004`.** Read it with `ethos mission show m-2026-09-08-004`. Write-set now includes `internal/mission/store.go`, `delegation.go`, their test files, `internal/mcp/mission_tools.go`, `format_output.go`, and `internal/hook/**`. Same branch, `fix/spawn-binding`, on top of `3cf6bf4`.

The contract funds exactly the design DES-076's Non-goal section recommends — bind-provenance field plus a narrowly-gated per-delegation disclaim. Don't redesign it from scratch. Do challenge it if implementation shows the recommendation was wrong; say so explicitly rather than diverging quietly.

Four things I added that weren't in your recommendation, all deliberate:

1. **The unknown-provenance case.** Delegations already on disk have no provenance field. An unknown value must NOT be treated as disclaimable — say in your result which direction you chose and why it's the safe one.
2. **Backward compatibility as a first-class requirement.** Verify against real on-disk records under `.punt-labs/ethos/missions/`, before and after, and paste the evidence. This repo is its own consumer.
3. **Security-review your own change.** You're adding an operator path that relaxes a deliberate guard. Can it retire a mission that genuinely had work done? Can a hand-edited provenance field on disk unlock it? Does a disclaim leave an audit record? "I found nothing" only counts if you say what you looked for.
4. **DES-076's PARTIAL marking goes stale the moment this lands.** Update the heading and the Non-goal section rather than appending a paragraph that contradicts them. An ADR saying two different things is worse than one saying nothing.

One constraint on my side: the guard in this session blocks `setsid` and `env` wrappers, so I can't run the detached test gate locally anymore — CI is now the authoritative no-Claude-ancestor check. If anything you write looks environment-sensitive, flag it explicitly so I watch for it in CI rather than discovering it in a review round.

**Re: the pre-existing staged file** — that's the cluster-2 mission's event log from when I closed `m-2026-09-08-001` while setting up your mission. It belongs in the commit; this repo's own rule is to commit mission logs when missions close. Good instinct to flag it rather than assume.

tool_input.name: rev-code
tool_input.prompt:
Review commit 3cf6bf4 on branch fix/spawn-binding in <repo>. Diff it against its parent 34f0e33 (`git diff 34f0e33..3cf6bf4`), ignoring the `.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/**` and `.punt-labs/ethos/missions/**` JSONL files — those are generated audit state, not authored code.

What the change does: `ethos mission dispatch` writes an "active-mission" sidecar that previously bound the NEXT `Agent()` spawn in the session to that mission, regardless of whether it was the intended worker. That silently mis-attributed unrelated agents as delegations of a mission they had nothing to do with. The fix makes the dispatch-origin binding single-use and scoped to the contract's declared `Worker`: only a spawn whose agent type matches consumes it; a mismatched spawn proceeds unbound and leaves the sidecar for the real worker. `ethos mission claim` bindings are deliberately unaffected and stay sticky.

The decision record is DES-076 in DESIGN.md — read it, and specifically check whether the code does what the ADR claims it does. On the PR that just merged in this repo, the single most expensive class of defect was prose asserting behavior the code did not have.

Focus areas, in priority order:

1. **Correctness of the match-and-consume logic.** `readActiveMissionForDispatch` and `consumeDispatchBinding` in `internal/hook/pretooluse_dispatch.go`. Is consumption correctly ordered relative to dispatch success? The ADR claims a spawn that gets blocked or hits an encode failure does NOT consume the binding, so retrying the same call still finds it — verify that's true in the code.
2. **The claim-vs-dispatch asymmetry.** `BindOriginClaim` must stay sticky; `BindOriginDispatch` must be single-use. Confirm the two paths cannot be confused, and that the origin file's ordering discipline described in `internal/mission/active.go` is preserved.
3. **CLAUDE.md compliance** for this repo — see the repo's CLAUDE.md and docs/development.md.
4. **Whether any comment or CLI output string now describes behavior the code no longer has.** The commit claims to fix one such string in `cmd/ethos/mission.go`. Check for others it missed.

Report concrete findings with file:line. If you find nothing in a category, say so explicitly rather than staying silent on it.

tool_input.name: rev-silent
tool_input.prompt:
Review commit 3cf6bf4 on branch fix/spawn-binding in <repo>. Diff against parent 34f0e33 (`git diff 34f0e33..3cf6bf4`), ignoring `.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/**` and `.punt-labs/ethos/missions/**` JSONL files — generated audit state, not authored code.

Context: this changes how `ethos mission dispatch`'s "active-mission" sidecar binds an `Agent()` spawn to a mission. Previously it bound the next spawn unconditionally, silently mis-attributing unrelated agents as delegations. Now it binds only a spawn whose agent type matches the contract's declared `Worker`, and consumes the binding on success.

This code sits in a PreToolUse hook, so it has a hard constraint the reviewer must weigh: **dispatch helpers must be non-blocking.** A failure here must not prevent the user's `Agent()` spawn from running. That means several error paths deliberately log to stderr and fall through rather than returning an error. Your job is NOT to flag every fallthrough as a silent failure — it is to judge whether each one is (a) genuinely justified by that constraint, (b) actually observable when it happens, and (c) failing in the safe direction.

Specific things to scrutinize:

1. **`readActiveMissionForDispatch`'s error paths** in `internal/hook/pretooluse_dispatch.go`. Several return `("", false)` after writing to stderr. For each: is the stderr message actionable — does it tell the operator what was bound, what happened, and what to do? Is there any path that returns the no-binding answer WITHOUT any diagnostic at all where one is warranted?

2. **The contract-load-failure case.** DES-076 says a contract that fails to load while gating a dispatch binding is treated as a mismatch, not a block, and explicitly acknowledges this diverges from the repo's own "malformed env never silently admits" doctrine. Read that justification in DESIGN.md and judge it. Is the divergence sound, and is the failure actually surfaced when it occurs? A deliberate, documented, observable divergence is fine; an undocumented or invisible one is not.

3. **`consumeDispatchBinding`.** If clearing the sidecar fails, what happens? A failure to consume means the binding survives and can capture a later spawn — the exact bug being fixed. Is that failure detected and reported, or swallowed?

4. **Anything that swallows an error while touching the audit trail.** In this project the audit trail is the product; a lost or wrong delegation record is data corruption, not a cosmetic issue.

Report findings with file:line and a concrete failure scenario for each. State explicitly which fallthroughs you examined and judged acceptable, with the reason — a clean report is only credible if it says what was checked.

tool_input.name: rev-invariant
tool_input.prompt:
Review commit 3cf6bf4 on branch fix/spawn-binding in <repo>. Diff against parent 34f0e33 (`git diff 34f0e33..3cf6bf4`), ignoring `.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/**` and `.punt-labs/ethos/missions/**` JSONL files — generated audit state.

This change and its ADR (DES-076 in DESIGN.md) make several claims about themselves. Your job is to verify each one actually holds in the code, not to trust the prose. The claims I want checked, verbatim from the ADR and commit message:

1. **"One dispatch, one binding, one consuming spawn — the sidecar cannot outlive the worker it was written for."** Is that exhaustively true? Enumerate the ways a dispatch-origin sidecar could persist past its intended worker and confirm each is handled or explicitly excluded. Consider: the worker never spawns at all; the worker spawns twice; the session ends mid-dispatch; two dispatches in a row before any spawn.

2. **"A spawn that gets blocked or hits an encode failure does not consume the binding, so a retry of the same `Agent()` call still finds it."** Verify against the actual ordering in `internal/hook/pretooluse_dispatch.go`, not the comment.

3. **`BindOriginClaim` "is unaffected: it stays sticky across every spawn until an explicit claim or release, exactly as before."** Confirm the claim path is genuinely untouched in behavior, and that no code path can convert one origin into the other.

4. **The declared-Worker match is the discriminator.** `spawnAgentType` reads `subagent_type` from tool input, falling back to `CLAUDE_AGENT_TYPE`. Is that the same answer `dispatchTierB` uses for its own delegation-skeleton write? The ADR claims both see the same answer for the same spawn — verify, because a divergence would mean the gate and the record disagree about who spawned.

5. **The regression test `TestDispatchAgent_ActiveMissionSidecarDispatchOrigin_MismatchedWorkerNotCaptured`.** Does it guard the general case, or only the specific arrangement it sets up? Specifically: would it still fail if someone reintroduced the bug in a slightly different way — say, by matching on the wrong field, or by consuming on mismatch instead of match? A test that passes only because of the exact fixture it built is not a regression gate.

6. **DES-076 is marked PARTIAL and its "Non-goal" section claims a specific residual case remains open: a spawn whose agent type equals the dispatched Worker but whose task is unrelated.** Confirm that is genuinely the ONLY residual, or name others the ADR failed to enumerate. An ADR that under-states what it leaves open is the defect I most want caught here.

Report each claim as CONFIRMED or not, with file:line evidence. Where a claim is only conditionally true, say under what condition it fails.
